title: Validate Binary Search Tree
summary: Return whether the whole tree satisfies strict binary search ordering.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–10,000 nodes. Values span the full signed 32-bit integer range. Repeated values cannot appear in a valid BST.

statement: Return whether the whole tree satisfies strict binary search ordering. Every value in a node's left subtree must be smaller than its value, and every value in its right subtree must be larger.

examples.explanation: 8 lies in the root's left subtree but exceeds 7.
Both subtrees satisfy the strict ordering.
The left child equals its parent.

constraints: 1–10,000 nodes. Values span the full signed 32-bit integer range. Repeated values cannot appear in a valid BST.
hints: Conceptual: A child can obey its parent's comparison while violating an earlier ancestor's bound.
Directional: A valid BST produces a strictly increasing sequence in inorder traversal.
Implementation: Visit left, node, then right. Reject a value at or below the previous visited value. Represent the absence of a previous value separately.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(h) auxiliary space for the traversal stack.
